finding: The v5 K562 source build and evaluation reproduced the prior source-only statistics exactly but are not accepted into the replacement chain.
The Arrow dataset scanner still decoded the one-row-group nested Orion Parquet columns too eagerly. The HCT116 process tree reached 22.18 GiB before batch 20 and the 18 GiB guard terminated it.
No HCT116 final donor directory was published. Stale lock files were removed only after the recorded process no longer existed.
A Polars 1.43.2 lazy streaming probe on the largest HCT116 file decoded all four required columns for 950 eligible cells at 3.83 GiB peak.

On HCT116_Batch106.parquet, the former whole-file reader and the Polars reader produced bit-identical SHA-256 hashes for the 613 by 4,992 response sums, target cell counts, and target total UMI. Peak RSS was 4.211 GiB for whole-file reading and 1.776 GiB for Polars.

correction.orion_reader: Use polars.scan_parquet with parallel none, low_memory true, rechunk false, cache false, the unchanged eligibility and target filters, and collect_batches with engine streaming and chunk_size 256.
correction.aggregation: Convert each returned small frame to Arrow and apply the unchanged float64 sparse target and response aggregation, then sum chunks within the same physical GEM-batch file.
correction.scientific_contract: Target eligibility, source rows, total UMI, response coordinates, duplicate-symbol rule, split assignments, arithmetic, reconstruction tolerance, operators, nulls, and gates remain unchanged.
